speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have right groin pain and your leg was positioned abnormally after a rear-end collision. Can you tell me exactly how your leg was positioned when you were first found by emergency services?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned immediate pain in both knees and severe right groin pain; did you experience any loss of sensation or inability to move your right leg or foot after the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Hip Fracture.

The description of your right leg being shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated is the classic presentation for a femoral neck fracture. Given the mechanism of injury and these specific physical findings, I need to confirm this with imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Hip X-Ray.
